dictionary.U001: As soon as anyone draws **End of Game**, the game ends immediately. Do not take Play actions or initiate trades after that draw. Make the **final payout for all owned lots and all casinos touching The Strip**, using normal money, boss-point and scoring-break rules. Highest score after that payout wins. If tied for most points, the tied player with **most money** wins. The source gives no further tiebreak if both remain equal.
dictionary.U002: In this base game, a player also **wins immediately at 90+ points**.
dictionary.U003: **Do not build on F block.** During setup, **discard any F-lot card and draw a replacement**; use the two accepted A–E cards for starting lots and money. Discarded F cards remain discarded.
dictionary.U004: During a turn, an **F-lot card places no marker**, but still causes the normal **owned-lot money and indicated casino money/points**. Discard it in its appropriate pile, then **repeat Draw** until an A, B, C, D or E card has been drawn and resolved. Only then proceed to Play. Thus multiple payouts can happen on one turn; you do not take actions between these draws. **End of Game still ends the game immediately** if drawn during this sequence.
dictionary.U005:
- **Casino tiles:** only 9 usable tiles per color. You cannot build or sprawl without the required available tile, or remodel without enough tiles of the chosen new color to replace the whole casino.
- **Ownership dice:** if all 12 of yours are already on the board when you must place one in a casino (including build, sprawl or inheriting a sprawled tile), **remove one of your dice from another tile and use it** at the value required by the new placement. The vacated tile stays, with no owner, and still counts toward its casino’s points. A casino with no dice has no owner/boss. You can trade to free a die. The limit applies to ownership placement; use any dice for gambling.
- **Lot markers:** if all 10 are on the board and you gain a new lot, move one of your markers to it; you cease to own the vacated lot.
- **Money:** the bank’s supply is unlimited. Your money, piece counts and discarded cards are public; anyone may inspect discard piles. A doubled gambling payout is limited by the boss’s available money, as stated above; action costs must be paid.
dictionary.U006: You must be **boss**. Choose a **new color with enough available tiles for the entire casino**. Pay **$5 per tile** and replace **every tile** of that casino with the new color, returning the old tiles to their supply. Dice stay with their holdings and keep their values. You cannot remodel just part of a casino.
dictionary.U007: Choose **a lot you own**. Take back its marker, choose an **available** casino tile of any color, pay the **price printed on the lot**, and place the tile there. Put one of your dice on it with the **lot’s printed die value** face up. Edge-connected same-color tiles merge immediately; boss control may change.
dictionary.U008: You must be **boss of the casino** you expand. Choose an **empty, unowned lot sharing an edge** with it, pay **twice that lot’s printed price**, and place an available tile of the **same color** there. Put your die on it at the **lot’s printed die value**. You cannot sprawl into another player’s marked lot, your own marked lot, a built space or a merely diagonal neighbor. Without an available tile of the required color, you cannot sprawl.
dictionary.U009:
- Board with lots grouped in blocks, The Strip, scoring track, wager area and property-card discard spaces.
- **9 usable casino tiles in each of 5 colors:** aqua, brown, gold, purple and silver. A tenth tile of each color is a replacement, not extra supply. Casino colors do not correspond to player colors.
- For each player: **12 dice, 10 translucent lot markers, a scoring chip and an action card**. Player colors are blue, green, red and yellow.
- Money, 49 property cards (including the End of Game card), player card and House card. The deck has **9 cards per casino color and 4 Pay The Strip cards**, including End of Game.
dictionary.U010:
1. **Draw a property card and take over its space before payouts.** If it is an empty lot, put your marker there. If it contains another player’s sprawled tile and die, replace their die with your own **at the same current pip value**, not the board’s printed value. If the tile has no die, add your die at the **printed board value**. If your own die already occupies it, leave it unchanged. The casino tile stays in place. Apply the dice/marker supply rules if necessary and settle any boss tie before paying casinos.
2. **All owned lots pay:** every lot with a marker pays its owner **$1 from the bank**, including the newly acquired lot, regardless of the card’s color or whose turn it is. Casino tiles do not also collect lot income.
3. **The indicated casinos pay money and points:** a single-color card pays every casino of that color anywhere on the board. A **Pay The Strip** card instead pays every casino with at least **one edge adjacent to The Strip**, regardless of color. A qualifying casino pays for **all its tiles**, not only the tile touching The Strip.
4. **Money:** each player receives **$1 per pip on each of their dice** in a paying casino, including players who are not its boss. **Points:** only the casino’s boss receives **1 point per tile** in that casino. Follow the scoring-break and separate-casino rules below.
5. Discard the property card in its appropriate color/Strip pile so the number already drawn remains countable. Proceed to Play, except that two-player F cards repeat Draw as described below.
dictionary.U011: Players may trade **at any time, even off-turn**, except during boss-tie resolution or after End of Game is drawn. Multiple players may participate. Trade any combination of **money, lots, dice in casinos and actions performed on the acting player’s current turn**.
dictionary.U012: For a transferred lot replace the owner’s marker with the recipient’s marker. For a transferred casino die replace it with the recipient’s die, retaining the **current pip value**, not the board’s printed die. A die trade can therefore change the boss and cause an immediate highest tie.
dictionary.U013: If **two or more players** tie for the **highest** value in a casino, reroll **all dice currently tied for highest**, **for free**. Leave smaller dice untouched. Reassess the highest value across the whole casino after each roll. If different players still tie for the current highest, reroll the current highest dice again. Continue until only **one player** owns the highest value; several highest dice belonging to that one player need no reroll.
dictionary.U014:
1. Pay **$1 per pip on every die in that casino**, including opponents’ dice, using their values before the roll.
2. **Reroll all dice**, not a chosen subset. Each player rolls their own dice.
3. Each player puts their rerolled dice back on **their own original tiles**. If they have multiple dice, they choose how to assign the rolled values among those tiles; they cannot move onto another player’s former tile. Temporary markers can help remember the original holdings.
dictionary.U015: No actions or initiated trades may interrupt the tie-resolution sequence. These free rerolls do not use up or reset a die’s paid-reorganization allowance.
dictionary.U016: You need **at least one die** in the casino; you **need not be boss** and may reorganize a casino containing only your dice.
dictionary.U017: **Once during your own turn**, choose a casino where **another player is boss**, and give that player the **House card**. If no opponent bosses a casino, you cannot gamble. You may bet no more than **all three limits**: **$5 per tile in that casino**, **your available money**, and **the boss’s available money**.
dictionary.U018: You **cannot trade points or casino tiles**, or promise actions, exchanges or transfers for **future turns**. **No player can perform an action on another player’s turn.** A current-turn action can be part of a trade only for the player whose turn it is. If something prevents an element of a trade from happening, the subsequent steps of that trade do not occur.
dictionary.U019:
1. Each player takes an action card and all pieces of one player color. Put every scoring chip on **0**. Choose a banker; put money and tiles within reach.
2. Remove **End of Game** from the property deck and shuffle the remaining cards. Deal **2 cards per player**. With two players, discard and replace any F-lot setup card, so each player receives two valid A–E initial properties.
3. Put one of your markers on each of your two initial lots. Take money from the bank equal to the **sum of the printed money values on your two cards**. These card money values apply **only during setup**. Discard the cards into their corresponding color/Strip spaces with counts easily visible.
4. Divide the remaining shuffled deck into **4 roughly equal stacks**. Put End of Game **on top of the fourth stack**, then put the other three stacks above it. Place the resulting draw pile beside the board.
5. Each player rolls **2 dice**. The highest roller takes the player card and the first turn. After each turn, pass it to the player on the **left**.

required_answer_facts: When an element of trade is prevented, subsequent steps do not occur.
Opponent cannot take action on your turn.
contextual_key_background: The scenario itself gives that failed boss control means the agreed sprawl cannot happen. This is not an independently asked rule in Q31; Q36 now explicitly tests boss-only sprawl eligibility.
effective_fixed_key.source_references: Unified p15 Trading; original p3 Sprawl/p4 Trading
effective_fixed_key.scope_note: The proposed sprawl is an intended action by the active player during this same turn. Question wording is preserved. No future-turn promise or off-turn action is authorized.
effective_fixed_key.expected_answer: When an element of trade is prevented, subsequent steps do not occur. Opponent cannot take action on your turn.

If the reroll does not make you boss so the agreed sprawl cannot happen, do the subsequent steps of the trade proceed? Could the opponent instead perform the sprawl on your turn?
required_answer_facts: When an element of trade is prevented, subsequent steps do not occur.
Opponent cannot take action on your turn.
contextual_key_background: The scenario itself gives that failed boss control means the agreed sprawl cannot happen. This is not an independently asked rule in Q31; Q36 now explicitly tests boss-only sprawl eligibility.
asked_scope.source_references: Unified p15 Trading; original p3 Sprawl/p4 Trading
asked_scope.scope_note: The proposed sprawl is an intended action by the active player during this same turn. Question wording is preserved. No future-turn promise or off-turn action is authorized.

a.answer: Trade may include a current-turn action, but only the turn player may perform it. Sprawl requires boss status. If something prevents an element of trade, subsequent steps do not occur. The opponent cannot sprawl on your turn.

b.answer: If reorganization does not make you boss and sprawl cannot happen, subsequent trade steps do not occur. Opponent cannot sprawl on your turn; only active player may perform traded action.

question.question: During setup, which pieces does each player take, and where is each player’s scoring chip placed before the first turn?

required_answer_facts: Each player takes an action card and the scoring chip, markers and dice of one player color. Place every player’s scoring chip on 0 on the scoring track.

question.question: Next to a casino you boss is an edge-adjacent, built casino tile of another color with no die. Is it a legal Sprawl target because it is unowned, or must the target be an empty lot?

effective_fixed_key.asked_question: Next to a casino you boss is an edge-adjacent, built casino tile of another color with no die. Is it a legal Sprawl target because it is unowned, or must the target be an empty lot?
required_answer_facts: No. A built casino tile remains on the board even without a die; it is a casino space, not an empty lot. Sprawl requires an empty, unowned lot, so you cannot sprawl onto or replace this tile.
effective_fixed_key.source_references: Original p2 Who Owns What; p3 Available Dice and Action–Sprawl; unified physicalp6 Available Dice and p10 Sprawl.
effective_fixed_key.scope_note: Origin boss and adjacency are givens; the asked distinction is unowned-but-occupied casino tile versus an empty lot. Different casino color is an ordinary legal scenario given preventing automatic preexisting merger, not an expansion effect.
effective_fixed_key.expected_answer: No. A built casino tile remains on the board even without a die; it is a casino space, not an empty lot. Sprawl requires an empty, unowned lot, so you cannot sprawl onto or replace this tile.
